collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Farmers want to set aside part of the harvest for families facing shortage: set it aside, or let each farmer decide.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Some families had a terrible season: sickness, a lost canoe, a garden washed away. (subject) wants every farmer to set aside part of the harvest for them. (friend) has had a poor year too, and would rather give what (friend.he/she) can, when (friend.he/she) can. What should the farmers do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Every farmer sets aside a share. It is left in the meeting hut, and families in need take it at night, so nobody has to be seen taking. Nobody goes hungry. (friend) gives less than the rest and nobody asks why.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: Each farmer gives what they choose. Some give a lot. Some give nothing. Two families have a very hard month. (subject) gives most of (subject.his/her) own harvest away, and goes hungry (subject.him/her)self for a while.
